forecasts.question: Will at least 50 commercial vessels per day transit the Strait of Hormuz (50%+ of pre-war ~120/day baseline) during any consecutive 7-day window before EOD 2026-06-10?
forecasts.delta_reason: Updated 0.38 → 0.14. PortWatch logged 4 commercial transits on 2026-05-24 against a pre-crisis baseline of 95-130/day — under 5% of normal, far below the 50-vessel threshold. All major carriers (Maersk, MSC, CMA CGM, Hapag-Lloyd) remain suspended. P&I war-risk insurance cancelled since March 5. 1,550+ vessels stranded. Even if an Iran-US framework were signed today, the operational sequence — carrier risk-assessment, Lloyd's premium reduction, route reinstatement, vessel repositioning, and 7 consecutive days at 50+ transits — cannot complete within 13 remaining days. Trump 'largely negotiated' (May 23) generated brief Brent decline to ~$96, but May 27 White House 'complete fabrication' statement and Trump 'won't be rushed' eliminated near-term deal confidence. Judge sets 0.14 (above Source A's 0.12 to credit non-zero surprise pathway; below Source B's 0.22-0.25 which overstates operational feasibility given transit ramp-up mechanics). Sources: USNI News, PortWatch 2026-05-24, CNBC, White House statement 2026-05-27.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if Hormuz Strait Monitor (or UNCTAD, or Lloyd's List) reports ≥50 daily transits averaged over 7 consecutive days within the horizon window. NO if average stays below 50/day for the full horizon window.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Hormuz Strait Monitor (primary), Lloyd's List Intelligence (secondary), UNCTAD Maritime Trade quarterly report (lagging confirmation).
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If only Iranian-flagged or sanctions-evading dark-fleet vessels make up the count, but Western insurers still refuse: AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO (the operationally meaningful question is whether Western shipping has returned). PGSA addendum (Judge, 2026-05-19): third-country vessels (Chinese, Indian, Turkish) transiting under Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority toll regime count ONLY IF ≥2 of Hormuz Strait Monitor/Lloyd's List/UNCTAD/Windward confirm them as independent commercial entities not under IRGC-linked tolls; PGSA self-reported numbers are excluded from resolution sourcing.

forecasts.question: Will Iran and the US confirm a signed written framework agreement (any named successor to the 14-point MOU) before EOD 2026-06-05?
forecasts.delta_reason: Updated 0.25 → 0.20. May 23 Trump 'largely negotiated' and May 24 Pezeshkian 'ready to assure the world' were positive data points. However, on May 27 the White House called the Iranian MOU leak 'a complete fabrication' and Trump told cabinet he is 'not satisfied with it yet' and 'won't be rushed.' These May 27 statements are the more recent and more dispositive evidence: they confirm the fabrication dispute broke the momentum generated by May 23-24 optimism. Substantive gaps remain on Hormuz sovereignty, nuclear sequencing, and sanctions relief. With 8 days to EOD June 5, the fabrication dispute and explicit no-rush posture reduce probability. Judge sets 0.20 — below Source A's 0.18 is defensible but 0.20 credits the genuine deal progress (Axios 14-point detail, Oman/Pakistan channel active) while accounting for the fabrication rupture. Source B's 0.40 substantially underweights the May 27 reversal. Sources: CNN, Axios (2026-05-24), White House statement (2026-05-27), NPR.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a named US administration official AND a named Iranian official publicly confirm a signed written framework (by any name); OR if the document text is published by Axios/Reuters/State Dept or Iran MFA with both parties acknowledging authenticity. Verbal 'agreement in principle' does not count.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: At minimum, Reuters AND one of Axios/AP/AFP quoting named US AND Iranian principals (not envoys alone). Official Iranian Foreign Ministry statement or State Dept press release also resolves.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Agreement by envoys only, without principal confirmation (Trump/Pezeshkian) within 72h of announcement = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. If Iran signs but Khamenei's office disavows within 72h = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. If SNSC formally blocks or delays implementation within 72h of signing = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. forecasts.question: Will Netanyahu formally announce an early election date earlier than the mandatory 2026-10-27 date before EOD 2026-06-01?
forecasts.delta_reason: Updated 0.22 → 0.08. Dissolution bill passed preliminary 110-0 on May 20 — but this is a first procedural reading; Israeli law requires three readings and a House Committee stage before a dissolution bill resolves. Haaretz (May 24) reports ultra-Orthodox parties (Degel HaTorah, Shas) yielded to Netanyahu's October 27 preference after Netanyahu revived the Haredi draft exemption bill as a side payment. Netanyahu separately told Haredim privately that September elections 'endanger' the right-wing bloc. No House Committee date scheduled. No public Netanyahu announcement of an earlier election date. With 4 days remaining, the formal resolution criteria — Netanyahu names a date before June 1 OR a Knesset dissolution vote passes — is structurally unreachable given coalition retreat to October. Judge sets 0.08 (above schema floor of 0.05 to credit black-swan scenario of surprise Netanyahu announcement; Source B's 0.33 misreads the legislative process by conflating preliminary reading with dissolution progress). Flagged: likely NO-resolution at EOD June 1. Sources: Haaretz 2026-05-24, Times of Israel, Jerusalem Post.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if Netanyahu makes a formal Knesset speech or public announcement naming an election date earlier than 2026-10-27; OR if the Knesset passes a formal dissolution motion by majority vote (third reading). Leaks and media speculation do NOT resolve.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Times of Israel, Haaretz, or Channel 12/13 news citing direct Netanyahu statement or official Knesset vote record. Reuters/AP confirmation required for international sources.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Coalition partner threatening dissolution without a formal Knesset vote = NOT resolved. Netanyahu 'considering' elections per aides = NOT resolved. Only a formal announcement by Netanyahu himself or a passed dissolution vote counts. First or second reading of dissolution bill does NOT resolve YES; only final passage (third reading) by majority vote counts. (Addendum 2026-05-28: multi-reading legislative clarification added per DA hygiene recommendation.)

forecasts.question: Will the Lebanon 45-day ceasefire extension (announced May 15) formally collapse — defined as US withdrawal of sponsorship OR Lebanese government publicly declaring the truce void — before EOD 2026-05-22?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-NO. The 45-day ceasefire extension, confirmed by the US State Department on May 15, remained formally in place through EOD May 22. No US State Department or Lebanese Foreign Ministry statement declared the truce void before the horizon. IDF operations in south Lebanon were severe — including significant strikes in Tyre, Nabatieh, and the Bekaa Valley — but the ambiguity rule explicitly excludes individual violations outside Beirut governorate from resolving YES. The IDF chief's 'no ceasefire' statement is operational military language, not a formal government withdrawal of sponsorship. The Soufan Center characterized the ceasefire as existing 'in name only' but no formal breakdown declaration was issued by either sponsoring party. Post-May 22 escalation (IDF strikes May 27 killing 31+, IDF chief restatement) does not retroactively resolve YES. Sources: PBS News (ceasefire extension), Al Jazeera War Day 89, US State Dept.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if the US State Department or Lebanese Foreign Ministry issues a public statement explicitly declaring the ceasefire void or withdrawn; OR if IDF and Hezbollah resume sustained exchange at pre-April-16 intensity (>50 launches/day from each side) and both US and Lebanon acknowledge breakdown. Individual violations — which are continuous — do NOT resolve YES.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: US State Dept press release or named spokesperson; OR Lebanese government official quoted in Reuters/AP/AFP; OR combined IDF/LBAF situation reports showing pre-truce intensity levels.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: IDF strikes in south Lebanon outside Beirut governorate = NOT collapse (consistent with current porous-truce pattern). Hezbollah verbal threat to resume without acting = NOT collapse. Collapse requires formal withdrawal of US or Lebanese government support.

indicators.expected_effect: +20pp toward YES; would demonstrate US tolerance for truce violation at capital level.

indicators.expected_effect: +15pp toward YES; mass rocket fire historically triggers Israeli large-scale response and truce void.

forecasts.question: Will the 45-day Lebanon ceasefire extension formally collapse — as declared void by the US State Department or Lebanese Foreign Ministry — before EOD 2026-06-10?
forecasts.delta_reason: Initial assignment. Replaces F4 (RESOLVED-NO). Since May 22: IDF struck 150+ targets on May 27 (31 killed, including children, in Tyre, Nabatieh, Bekaa); Hezbollah drones reached Rosh Hanikra and Shlomi; IDF chief stated 'there is no ceasefire in south Lebanon'; Netanyahu said Israel is 'deepening our operation' with ground forces. Ben-Gvir called for return to 'large-scale combat' on May 25. These factors collectively put a formal breakdown within the resolution criteria at roughly 0.42 probability. The countervailing factor is significant: the US has not issued a formal void declaration, and Trump almost certainly needs the ceasefire framework intact as diplomatic cover for the concurrent Iran MOU process — a formal US declaration of Lebanon ceasefire collapse would undermine that track. This structural tension between military reality and diplomatic cover holds the probability below 0.50. Sources: Al Jazeera War Day 89 (2026-05-27), IDF statements, PBS News.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if US State Dept or Lebanese FM issues official statement explicitly declaring ceasefire void or ended; OR if both IDF and Hezbollah officially acknowledge in statements that full combat resumed at pre-April-16 intensity, verified by UN UNIFIL or OCHA reporting >50 launches per side per day sustained over 3+ days.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: US State Dept official statement (state.gov), Lebanese FM official statement, or UN UNIFIL/OCHA situation reports, confirmed by Reuters or AP within 24 hours.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Individual IDF strikes, even mass-casualty, do not resolve YES without formal void declaration. IDF chief statements about 'no ceasefire' do not resolve YES unless accompanied by formal government declaration. Hezbollah drone attacks without IDF acknowledgment of ceasefire end do not resolve YES.
